- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast by 1–2% to reflect sharper decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a lagged correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment divergence.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
